ns0:entry.ns0:title: docs(robocasa): fix camera rename_map for smolvla_robocasa (#4860)
ns0:entry.ns0:content:
docs(robocasa): fix camera rename_map for smolvla_robocasa (#4860)

The RoboCasa365 eval snippets and the RoboCasa CI command mapped
`robot0_eye_in_hand` to `camera2` and `robot0_agentview_right` to
`camera3`, swapping the wrist and right agent views relative to how
`lerobot/smolvla_robocasa` was trained.

The checkpoint's own `train_config.json` and `policy_preprocessor.json`
both record `robot0_agentview_left` -> `camera1`,
`robot0_agentview_right` -> `camera2`, `robot0_eye_in_hand` -> `camera3`.
Since `--rename_map` replaces the checkpoint preprocessor's rename step
and all three views are 3x256x256, the mismatch was silently accepted.

ns0:entry.ns0:title: feat(optim): add opt-in fused Adam/AdamW flag (#5023)
ns0:entry.ns0:content:
feat(optim): add opt-in fused Adam/AdamW flag (#5023)

Fused Adam/AdamW kernels can shorten the optimizer step of large
policies, but there was no way to request them: policy presets
replace --optimizer.* and AdamWConfig had no fused field.

Add fused to AdamConfig and AdamWConfig and expose it as
optimizer_fused on act, groot, pi0, pi0.5, pi0_fast and smolvla.
The default stays None so PyTorch keeps choosing its implementation
(foreach on CUDA); a False default would force the slower for-loop
path instead.

A resumed run rebuilds its optimizer from the checkpoint's config, so
optimizer_fused has no effect there, as the docs now say. Overriding
--optimizer.fused between None and a bool on resume fails the
optimizer state load.

Co-authored-by: Pepijn <138571049+pkooij@users.noreply.github.com>

ns0:entry.ns0:content:

running accumulator.

ns0:entry.ns0:title: feat(dataset-viz): show the language task in the Rerun viewer (#4322)
ns0:entry.ns0:content:
feat(dataset-viz): show the language task in the Rerun viewer (#4322)

* feat(dataset-viz): show the language task in the Rerun viewer

The Rerun viewer logs images, action, state, done, reward and success, but never
the natural-language task. That leaves the one field a VLA is actually
conditioned on as the only one you cannot see while inspecting a dataset, which
makes it easy to miss wrong or ambiguous instructions.

Log it as a Markdown TextDocument under a `task` entity, re-logged only when the
string changes, so scrubbing shows the instruction in effect at that point
instead of writing one entry per frame.

The blueprint puts it in a thin banner above the existing grid
(`row_shares=[1, 9]`) rather than giving it a grid cell of its own: it is a
single line of text, so a full cell would waste space and break up the camera
layout.

Guarded by `if "task" in batch`, so datasets without a task are unaffected.

* Remove TASK_ENTITY constant from dataset visualization

Removed TASK_ENTITY constant definition from the script.

* Add TASK constant to constants.py

* Add TASK constant and update task logging

ns0:entry.ns0:title: fix(scripts): don't crash lerobot-info when a package fails to import…
ns0:entry.ns0:content:
fix(scripts): don't crash lerobot-info when a package fails to import (#4935)

get_package_version() only caught ImportError. torchcodec raises
RuntimeError when it can't load its FFmpeg libraries, so lerobot-info
exited with a traceback instead of printing the system summary, which is
when users need it most (e.g. Jetson Thor with JetPack 7, whose system
FFmpeg has no libavdevice).

Packages that are installed but fail to import are now reported as
"<version> (import failed: <error type>)".

ns0:entry.ns0:content:
fix(envs): explain that gym_manipulator cannot be built by make_env (#4997)

`lerobot-eval --env.type=gym_manipulator` (or make_env with
HILSerlRobotEnvConfig) failed with "Package 'gym_gym_manipulator' required for
env 'gym_manipulator' not found", sending users after a package that does not
exist. The environment drives a physical robot and is built by
lerobot.rl.gym_manipulator.make_robot_env.

HILSerlRobotEnvConfig.create_envs now raises NotImplementedError naming the
commands to use instead.

ns0:entry.ns0:title: fix(tests): restore torch.backends flags after real train() calls (#4…
ns0:entry.ns0:content:
fix(tests): restore torch.backends flags after real train() calls (#4748)

train() unconditionally flips torch.backends.cudnn.benchmark/deterministic
and cuda.matmul.allow_tf32; these are process-global, so any test calling
train() for real leaks them into whatever test runs next in the same
pytest session. #4740 fixed one instance (flux3 lora, allow_tf32 only);
this covers the same test's cudnn flags plus two more affected files
(test_ema.py, test_visual_validation.py) via an autouse restore fixture.

ns0:entry.ns0:title: fix(datasets): warn only when the dataset is newer than the codebase …
ns0:entry.ns0:content:
fix(datasets): warn only when the dataset is newer than the codebase (#4852)

check_version_compatibility compared minor versions without checking which
side is newer, so a dataset older than the codebase (v3.0 dataset, v3.1 code)
was reported as "only available in 3.0 format ... please update lerobot",
while a dataset written by a newer release was accepted silently.

The check now only acts when the dataset is newer than the codebase: a newer
minor version warns as before, and a newer major version raises
ForwardCompatibilityError (the class already exists for that purpose and is
used by get_safe_version). Older-minor datasets stay silent, and a v2.1
dataset read by v3 code still raises BackwardCompatibilityError.

Fixes #4851
